meta.name: First Interaction — Glider meets Block
meta.description: The riskiest assumption test: does a glider traveling across a medium grid meaningfully reach and interact with a block, and does the result produce a legible ownership outcome that a human player could reason about?
meta.rules: Standard Conway + majority-of-parents ownership, advanceSteps=4 so each turn moves a glider by exactly 1 diagonal cell
questions: Does a glider meaningfully travel across a 12x12 in a reasonable number of turns?
When a glider hits a block, is the outcome visually legible?
Does the ownership propagation feel natural (debris colored by parent majority)?
Does this scenario feel like a game where decisions matter?

moves.note: P2 opens aggressively — a glider launched from the NW corner heading SE. This is a long-range attack that will take several turns to reach the middle of the board.
P1 responds defensively, planting a block in the center where the glider is heading. A block is a still life — it will sit there until something disturbs it.
First time step. Glider should advance 1 diagonal cell, block should be stable.
P1 reinforces with a second block adjacent to the first, trying to build a wall. Risk: adjacent blocks may interact in weird ways rather than staying stable.
P2 sends a second glider from further down the left edge, also heading SE. Wants to hit the block wall from a different angle.
No placements — both players watching the gliders travel. Pure observation turn.
Glider 1 should now be close to the block wall. Impact should happen this turn or next.
